text:
emma: noticing a spike of 503s from hosted inference in us-west-2 starting ~12:02 UTC. multiple customers reporting timeouts / 5xx. root logs show repeated worker exits (segfault / OOM) and container restarts. hitting support escalations already.

raj: looking now — can you paste one of the worker logs/stack traces? is this tied to model swap or a batch size change?

emma: pasting the short excerpt we grabbed from a crashing pod: ```
[2026-03-10T12:02:14Z] infer-worker[1234]: ERROR Unhandled exception: SIGSEGV at 0x7f8a2c3b
[2026-03-10T12:02:14Z] infer-worker[1234]: GPU0: cudaMalloc failed: out of memory trying to allocate 2147483648 bytes
[2026-03-10T12:02:15Z] watcher: container restart count=5 (last exit: OOM)
stacktrace: 0x7f8a2c3b -> 0x7f8a3050 -> 0x400f9a
```

marta: CS already flagging 3 tenants: acme-co, pulseai, and demo-app. billing noticed a retry storm and duplicated token usage for some calls. CS wants an ETA before we open debt/credit tickets.

alex: FYI we rolled a change to the batcher earlier today (deploy abc123) that tweaks prefetch size and dyn-batching thresholds. I reverted the config on a canary node but haven't rolled full rollback.

raj: ok. two lines of investigation: 1) confirm whether kernel-level OOM (driver) or allocator-level; check dmesg / nvidia logs on node; 2) reproduce locally with same model+batch mix. can someone grab the node id for one affected pod?

emma: node: ip-10-0-7-142.us-west-2, pod: infer-runner-7f9d8 (container id: containerd://sha256:9a8b...). dmesg shows repeated "Out of memory: kill process" around crash time.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: detected high restart rate for infer-runner-7f9d8, flagged for manual review. autoscaler suppressed new allocations due to repeated OOMs.

raj: thanks. grabbing kernel logs and nvml outputs now. initial glance suggests GPU memory leak in the attention kernel under high prefix length + dynbatch. putting a temporary mitigation: reduce per-request max_tokens and cap batch size to 4 for us-west-2.

alex: pushed a short config patch to limit dynbatch max_batch=4 on us-west-2 (hotfix cfg-2026-03-10). rolling to 20% of cluster now.

marta: can we give CS a mitigation note: disable retries client-side and reduce concurrency; we'll provide credits if usage was inflated due to our retries? support-bot, can you create a ticket for each affected tenant and link this thread?

support-bot: created tickets: TCK-4521 (acme-co), TCK-4522 (pulseai), TCK-4523 (demo-app). assigned to emma and cs-ops.

raj: reproduction notes so far: running model redwood-open-7b q4_0 with prefix length 2048 and dynbatch enabled + prefetch on a single GPU reproduces OOM after ~30s at batch sizes >=8. workarounds: 1) reduce batch to <=4, 2) disable kv-prefetch, 3) force model-variant quantized fallback.

emma: CS told customers to switch to smaller model temporarily and we disabled prefetch for affected tenants. early metrics show 503s decreasing but error rate still elevated.

alex: logging shows a small number of SIGSEGV frames tied to fused attention kernel at high sequence lengths. I'll open an ops-jira for kernel revert and coordinate with runtime team.

raj: next steps: 1) full rollback of today's batcher config if hotfix doesn't drop error rate to baseline in next 15m; 2) collect full core dumps and GPU nvcrash logs for 3 nodes and upload to s3://redwood-incident-dumps/1768421111/; 3) create a postmortem if any customer experienced >5% p95 latency regression or billing anomalies.

marta: flagged priority postmortem and customer communications. drafting a CS note: short-term mitigation (reduced batches, disable prefetch), ETA for fix (TBD after debug).

emma: timeline so far: 12:02 detected -> 12:08 hotfix deployed -> 12:15 partial improvement -> 12:20 still seeing sporadic crashes on 2 nodes. continuing triage. I'll update thread every 15min. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

alex: added link to rollback PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ops/PR/789 (internal).

raj: uploaded nvml logs and dkms dmesg snippets to the s3 bucket. pointer: s3://redwood-incident-dumps/1768421111/nvml-node-10-0-7-142.log

infra-bot: monitor: routing fallback to cpu-pool enabled for bursts; fallback activated three times.

marta: CS wants a customer-facing summary once we have root cause. for now we'll advise credits for excess tokens caused by retries. please tag me when postmortem is ready.

emma: updating support tickets and adding repro steps. will follow up in 15.

-- end of thread --
